To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrate a facile one-step method to produce versatile, highly ordered microstructures in a controlled environment.

the evaporation of a nonvolatile solute from a capillary bridge confined in curve-on-flat geometry can produce highly ordered structures that are precisely controlled by the upper surface geometry, and the structures are robust, reproducible, and scalable over large areas.

the use of a confined curve–on-flat geometry results in a simple, robust, one-step, and highly controllable means of evaporative self-organization of nonvolatile solvents into highly ordered structures over large surface area.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a robust and facile method of fabricating highly ordered structures by evaporation of confined polymer solutions.
the formation of complex, highly ordered structures by controlled evaporative self-assembly.
the fabrication and control of complex, self-assembled structures by evaporation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the evaporation-induced self-organization process in the confined curve-on-flat geometrical environment can be used to create a wide variety of highly ordered, complex, and versatile microstructures, including square stripes, triangular contour lines and ellipses, as well as the ability to control the number of rings in concentric rings.
this work demonstrates the feasibility of using a curve-on-flat geometry to produce a diverse range of complex, ordered structures in a controlled manner.

the evaporation process is highly complex and is governed by a number of factors, including the shape and size of the upper surface, the surface tension of the solution, the evaporation rate of the solvent, the surface roughness of the upper surface and substrate, the contact angle, and the capillary force.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a facile, cost-effective, robust method to create a diverse range of highly ordered, complex structures by precisely controlling the evaporation of nonvolatile materials in a confined microfluid environment that is guided by the shape (e.g., the square, triangular, and chisel) of the upper surface of the curve-on-flat geometrical system.
the evaporation of a polymer solution confined in a curve-on-flat geometry can be used to create a wide range of self-assembled complex structures.
the upper surface of the confined microfluids is the key for controlling the evaporation process, and thus, for the self-assembly of the nonvolatile solutes into highly ordered complex patterns.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the controlled self-assembly of complex structures by solvent evaporation is a robust, facile, and scalable process that can be tailored by simply varying the upper surface of a curve-on-flat geometry to produce a wide range of self-organized structures with well-controlled spatial arrangements.
the controlled evaporation of polymer solutions in a curve-on-flat geometry is an effective and robust method of producing highly ordered complex structures.
the use of a confined microfluid in a curve-on-flat geometry provides a facile, cost-effective, one-step method to produce highly regular complex structures.
